note: #3092 asks for the SPIR-V workgroup size to be driveable by a Vulkan specialization constant. The symptom of the capability being absent is a DIAGNOSTIC, so the diagnostic text is written in verbatim rather than approximated -- SKILL.md step 6 (`_predicate_quotes`) needs the exact string, and an approximation would be scored differently by the invalid-probe classifier. Measured wording, identical on v1.5.2010, v1.6.2104, v1.7.2207, v1.8.2403, v1.8.2505, v1.9.2607 and main-debug: `repro.hlsl:14:2: error: 'numthreads' attribute requires an integer constant`. NOT an absence predicate: it asserts output the compiler had to produce, so it cannot be satisfied for free by a run that failed early. CONTROLS (both --expect no-match, both captured): control-static-const.hlsl replaces the spec constant with a `static const uint` -- it compiles clean and emits `OpExecutionMode %main LocalSize 4 1 1`, so the predicate is not firing on 'a named constant appears in numthreads'; control-specconst-literal.hlsl declares and uses the same `[[vk::constant_id(1)]]` constant with a literal numthreads -- it compiles clean, so the predicate is not firing on 'a spec constant is present'. KNOWN LIMIT, guarded by a linear bisect rather than by the predicate: if some release accepted the attribute and silently folded the spec constant to its initialiser, it would emit no diagnostic and score no-repro, which would read as a fix. `SemaHLSL.cpp:13858 ValidateAttributeIntArg` makes that shape plausible (it looks up the VarDecl and constant-folds `decl->getInit()`). Every release was therefore probed linearly and every capture checked for a literal `LocalSize` with no `LocalSizeId`; see notes.md. match-no-spec-link.json measures the capability itself and covers both shapes.
